blockerB.sourceOfTheGrant: Supabase default privileges. Both ACLs read anon=rwU/postgres and authenticated=rwU/postgres — held DIRECTLY, not through PUBLIC (has_sequence_privilege('public', …) was false). No migration granted them: the Preview lineage that created the sequences carried no privilege block, and Supabase projects carry `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on sequences to anon, authenticated, service_role`. This is the sequence-shaped twin of the function-privilege defect repaired in 202608010001/202608010104.

terminalEvidenceRemediation.reason: The technical blockers were closed, but three evidence/truth defects remained. All three are same-package defects of mine, recorded here rather than erased.

defects.defect: the sequence negative control claimed verifier failure but never ran the verifier
defects.detail: the test named 'stale sequence grants make promotion verification fail' only asserted that supabase/contracts/por1-promotion-contract.json does not itself list anon/authenticated grants. That is a statement about a checked-in file, not about the gate — it would have passed even if verify-promoted-contract.mjs contained no sequence check at all.
defects.remediation: replaced with a real subprocess control that runs the SHIPPED CLI over two synthetic catalogues built from the contract's own objects, so the only variable is the sequence usage_grants string. The verifier's logic is neither mocked nor reimplemented.

defects.defect: PR #126's FIRST identity block remained stale and contradictory
defects.detail: the block at the top of the PR body still read 'Hosted acceptance PASSED at the exact head below' with Head de40edd — from the original CPC-1 submission. The previous package corrected a LATER identity table and appended to the body instead of fixing the first one, so the PR simultaneously claimed the current head had and had not passed hosted acceptance.
defects.remediation: the first block is replaced in place with current head / last hosted application acceptance head (a1cf81c) / Production main (c8d8a8ad) / current-head hosted application acceptance: NOT YET RUN. The CPC-1 hosted evidence is retained but explicitly labelled historical.

defects.defect: build-final-contract.sh contradicted itself about Supabase default privileges
defects.detail: the header stated the disposable clusters carry 'the Supabase platform roles AND Supabase's default privileges' while prepare() deliberately omits the default privileges — a decision made mid-package and documented in the body but not in the header.
defects.remediation: header corrected: the clusters carry the Supabase-equivalent PLATFORM ROLES; they deliberately do NOT install default privileges; the contract records the end state established by repository migrations; environment-level default-privilege behaviour is asserted by the migration assertions (202608010108) and by Supabase-shaped rehearsals.
